 New Zealand A tail frustrate India A 
 Mukesh takes 5, Siraj 4 wickets in second Test
 Mukesh Kumar 
 Agencies
 Nov 03, 2026 01:00 PM | UPDATED: Nov 03, 2026 02:13 AM | 8 min read 
 #Christchurch
 Pacer Mohammed Siraj warmed up for the upcoming two-Test series with four wickets in 35 overs for India A but New Zealand A’s lower order showed a lot of grit to earn a 78-run first innings lead on the penultimate day of the second Test here. 
   Replying to India A’s first innings score of 346, New Zealand A, who were reduced to 338 for 8, finished their first innings at 424. 
    The last two wickets yielded 86 runs to provide the hosts a handy lead.
 Speedster Siraj took 4/118 in 35 overs while seamer Mukesh Kumar grabbed 5 for 87 in 29 overs to share the bulk of the spoils.
 At stumps, India A reached 32 for no loss in their second innings with Yashasvi Jaiswal (20 batting) and Sai Sudharsan (11 batting) negotiating the remaining 11 overs of the day safely. For the Indian senior team support staff, Siraj adding miles to his legs at a venue where the team will play the second Test against New Zealand is certainly a big positive. 
 The Test series against the Black Caps begins on November 19. Bowling 35 overs is the kind of workout that head coach Gautam Gambhir and Morne Morkel would be pleased with before Siraj links up with the ODI squad at the end of this game. He looked sharp even with the old ball and was incisive with the new one. His seam bowling partner Mukesh was good with both the first and second new ball but not so much when the Kookaburra became semi-new and subsequently old. Siraj got a wicket with his very first delivery on the third morning. It was the second over of the day and overnight centurion Matthew Boyle (110, 152 balls) got one that shaped away after pitching and Devdutt Padikkal dived full stretch to his left to snap it up.  
 Brief Scores: India A 1st Innings 346 and 32 for no loss (Yashasvi Jaiswal 20 batting). New Zealand  A 1st Innings 424 (Matthew Boyle 110, Dean Foxcroft 93, Mukesh Kumar 5/87, Mohammed Siraj 4/118).  Agencies
